rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's urgent wish that his people believe and escape punishment shows affection and honour for truth, but remains bounded by God's established practice.
rows.anchor: These emotions bear witness to his affection and to the honour he has for the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a messenger appears to exceed the limits of God's practice, God intervenes to stop him.
rows.anchor: If it appears that a messenger may exceed these limits, the Almighty takes the initiative in stopping him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for listening means listening with understanding; hearing without understanding does not count as true listening.
rows.anchor: is used in its complete meaning ie, to listen and understand. Those who listen but do not understanding are ones who actually do not listen.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead are those whose intellect and heart are lifeless, since real life consists in their being alive.
rows.anchor: The word “dead” refers to those who whose intellect and heart are dead.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent rebuke of the Prophet conceals affection; any harshness targets the wretched evaders whose rejection made him anxious.
rows.anchor: There exists an apparent rebuke in these verses for the Prophet (sws). However, there is great affection concealed in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet wanted the demanded miracle to remove the rejecters' excuses, but God does not intend to make people believe through miracles.
rows.anchor: He wanted that the miracle they were demanding be shown to them so that they were left with no excuse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wants people to reflect on signs with their senses and intellect, listen to the Prophet, and believe by free choice; He could force belief instantly but chose not to.
rows.anchor: He wants them to use their ears, eyes and intellect and reflect on the signs found with them and around them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not let his emotions obscure God's practice and mercy concerning faith.
rows.anchor: So the Prophet (sws) should not be so overwhelmed with emotions that he loses sight of God’s practice and mercy in this matter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign here may refer to any of the signs the disbelievers demanded from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: The “sign” here can refer to any of the signs the disbelievers demanded from the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters treated the requested sign as amusement, unaware that its manifestation would devastate them.
rows.anchor: They regarded it to be a matter of mere amusement and jest. The fact is that if such a sign did manifest itself, it would break their backs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's practice is to give rejecters respite until the truth is fully established, then seize them beyond anyone's power to rescue.
rows.anchor: He gives them respite until a certain time period so that the truth is conclusively communicated to them in every respect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respite is neither evidence that the threat is false nor that God is helpless; His planning is sound and no one escapes His eventual grasp.
rows.anchor: God gives respite to the rebellious and hence His planning is very-well founded.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respite is also an expression of mercy: God keeps repentance and reform open until creatures close that door through stubbornness.
rows.anchor: He keeps the door of repentance and reformation open as long as His creatures do not close them due to their stubbornness and obduracy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 38 omits parallel phrases: “on earth” supplies “in the sky,” while “fly on both their wings” supplies “roam on their legs.”
rows.anchor: fly on both their wings) in the second part of the sentence, a suppression of its parallel expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise description of animals as communities like humans redirects sign-seekers to the abundant signs in the universe, where every living creature witnesses to God.
rows.anchor: The attention of those who were demanding signs is directed towards the signs around them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living creatures are signs of God, and their individual and collective existence displays providence, wisdom, and power attesting to monotheism, reward, punishment, and the Messenger's truth.
rows.anchor: numerous signs of God’s providence, wisdom and power that bear witness to monotheism, reward and punishment and the veracity of the messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each species has awareness of its collective life, forming an organized unit whose members preserve it and help fulfil its purpose.
rows.anchor: each species has an awareness of its collective existence that induces it to live as an organized unit and also preserve its unity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an cites the honeybee as an example of signs of its Creator's providence, wisdom, and power in animal communities.
rows.anchor: In S ūrah al-Naḥl, the Qur’ ān has mentioned the honey-bee as an example

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instinctive traits in bees and ants—including care, protection, planning, division of labour, hierarchy, provisioning, intelligence, and self-sacrifice—are astonishing signs.
rows.anchor: How splendid is their diligence in nourishing their young ones, vigilance in securing themselves from dangers, foresight in planning for future circumstances

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of creaturely life points to a Creator and planner who continues to govern it, a single wise and merciful God rather than autonomous forces or rival deities.
rows.anchor: is there a creator and planner behind it? If latter is the case, then has the creator become aloof after creating all this or is He directly governing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe's purpose and design point toward a grand purpose and eventual accountability before its powerful, wise Creator, rather than a life without responsibility.
rows.anchor: Does it seem to be a purposeless and meaningless place having no purpose or does it have a grand purpose that shall definitely manifest itself?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unperverted human nature and sound intellect must accept the second option in these reflections; every particle and creature testifies to it, so no miracle is needed.
rows.anchor: If the nature of a human being has not been perverted and if his intellect has not been paralyzed, then he is forced to confess that the second option

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an merely invites people to accept what the universe already demonstrates, and creatures on land and in the sky testify to its truth.
rows.anchor: then the Qur’ ān is only inviting people to accept it. So, why is a miracle needed to accept what it says?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who ignores evidence within himself can still look to the external signs around him.
rows.anchor: If a person has shut his eyes to the evidence found in his own being, he can at least open them to see the signs found outside him.

rows.speaker: people
rows.claim: Many readers understand “Book” as the register where people's deeds are recorded.
rows.anchor: People mostly think that the word “book” in verse 38 to refers to the register in which the accounts of people is maintained.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, Islahi repeatedly inclines to understand “Book” as the Qur'an: like the universe, it fully presents arguments for the Messenger's message, in varied styles that the dead-hearted cannot grasp.
rows.anchor: keeping in view the context, my mind is repeatedly inclined to infer that it means the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering before the Lord is a sarcastic warning: signs fill both universe and scripture, but the unwilling will only open their eyes at the gathering.
rows.anchor: The words “then all of them will be gathered before their Lord” sarcastically refer to the fact that as far as signs are concerned both the universe and the scripture are replete with them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are blind, deaf, and dumb cannot be cured in this world.
rows.anchor: These blind, deaf and dumb people cannot be cured in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance follows an established practice: He does not force guidance on those who shut their eyes and ears, and guides those willing to use their faculties.
rows.anchor: God does not force His guidance into those who do not open their eyes and ears.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two expressions cited are synonymous, and the expression in verse 45 is used in the same way.
rows.anchor: are synonymous in meaning. Thus in verse 45

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses answer the demand for a punishment-sign and argue for monotheism: when punishment or the Hour comes, people call only on God, who alone may relieve them, and they forget their partners.
rows.anchor: Will they call upon someone other than God if they are actually sent such a sign? The fact is that they will never call their deities for help

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature attests to one God alone; other deities have no basis in it, so in severe trials people forget these hypothetical gods and plead only with God.
rows.anchor: the basic premise in this regard is that human nature bears witness to one God only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadarruʿ means the heart's humble, devoted submission to God; its opposite, hardness, entails arrogance and lack of fear.
rows.anchor: signifies bowing before God with all the humility, devotion and servitude. Here it refers to humility, devotion and servitude of the heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses describe God's established practice for punishing nations sent messengers: those demanding a sign as a condition of belief never believe and are ultimately routed.
rows.anchor: nations which demand a sign as a condition for accepting faith were never fortunate enough to accept faith and were ultimately routed by Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected earlier nations to financial and bodily trials to awaken fear and warn that rejecting their messenger would bring decisive punishment; instead their hearts hardened, Satan beautified their deeds, and they persisted.
rows.anchor: previous nations towards whom messengers were sent were put through various trials to instil the fear of God in them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the nations were reminded by refers to financial and bodily trials warning that rejection of the messenger would be followed by decisive punishment.
rows.anchor: The expression “that through which they had been reminded” refers to the financial and corporeal trials God had inflicted them with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They dismissed famine, floods, storms, and epidemics as ordinary calamities faced by every nation instead of treating them as warnings for rejecting a messenger.
rows.anchor: They reckoned that calamities such as famine, floods, storms and endemics are faced by every nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the doors of everything marks the next phase of God's established practice toward those nations.
rows.anchor: The words “We opened the doors of everything to them until just as they were showing conceit on what they were given, We suddenly seized them” state the next phase of the afore-mentioned established practice of God.
